ghi: THAM KHẢO — không phải chấm đạt; chủ dự án chấm cuối (§13.4)

tra_loi.Q1: A huge city fire. The date counter reads 2 Sept 1666 and the caption says 'The Great Fire'. Timber-framed houses burn, with thick smoke over the city and the river.
tra_loi.Q2: It begins in one small place. A baker's (Thomas Farriner, baker to the King) oven fire and sparks set a narrow street alight (frames 22-23). The fire then spreads along the north bank of the river to cover a big area over several days (2-5 Sept).
tra_loi.Q3: People flee on foot with bundles, pile belongings onto horse carts, and escape in rowing boats on the river (frames 48-50). Some crowds camp in open fields with tents and campfires (frames 72-73). Some men pull down houses with hooks and ropes to make firebreaks (frame 40), and a house is blown up (frame 68). Two men bury items in a garden (frames 69-70).
tra_loi.Q4: The huge Gothic church on the hill, shown on screen with a caption naming Old St Paul's, catches fire on 4 Sept. Its windows blaze, molten lead or fire runs down the walls and along the street, and it is gutted (frames 59-65). By frame 85 the ruins include a toppled statue.
tra_loi.Q5: It is rebuilt in red brick, with new brick houses going up (frames 95-96, 98-99). The caption says 'Rebuilding on the old streets', so the layout is the old street pattern, not a new plan (frames 83-90). Maps with Wren's plan are shown, but the new streets seem to follow the old ones.
tra_loi.Q6: A large white domed cathedral rises above the red roofs. The caption reads 'The dome rules the skyline' (1711), and '365 ft' flashes on screen. A tall column (the Monument) appears in several skyline shots, but I'm not sure which frame is which.
tra_loi.Q7: On 29 Dec 1940 the city is bombed (night raids, airships/planes over an empty street) and burns again, called 'the second great fire'. Firefighters work along the river and on rooftops. The dome of St Paul's survives, shown in a 1942 photo (frame 160) and circled in the 1938 frames. Large areas around it are destroyed. The map marks '160 killed'.
tra_loi.Q8: A modern 2026 city of glass and concrete towers and office blocks beside the river with bridges. The old domed cathedral is still visible among the skyscrapers (frames 176, 180-181). At night the city is lit by windows (frames 184-190). The film ends with a 'How this film was made' text card.

tra_loi.Q1: A huge fire (the Great Fire, dated 2 Sept 1666) burns through a crowded city of timber houses beside a river. The fire spreads for days, with dates counting from 2 to 5 Sept 1666.
tra_loi.Q2: It seems to start in one small place. A baker's shop (Thomas Farriner, baker to the King) shows a glowing oven and sparks, and the fire then catches in a narrow street. After that it spreads across a big stretch of the riverside city, with smoke over the old London Bridge area. The pictures do not show the exact starting spot, so I am not sure of that.
tra_loi.Q3: People pack bundles and loaded carts and flee along the streets. Others row away on the river in boats with their goods. Men pull down houses with hooks and ropes, and one house is blown up, to make firebreaks. A Lord Mayor and a diarist appear as officials and witnesses. One pair bury valuables in a garden pit, and refugees camp in fields with tents and bundles outside the burning city.
tra_loi.Q4: The big Gothic church on the hill (shown on the 4 Sept frames, marked as Old St Paul's) catches fire. Its windows blaze, and what looks like molten lead streams down the walls and runs across the street. It is burned and ruined, and a statue lies among the rubble afterwards.
tra_loi.Q5: The city is rebuilt in red brick. Frames show brick houses going up with bricklayers, scaffolding and carts. The caption says 'Rebuilding on the old streets', so the old street pattern is kept and the rebuilt streets follow the old map. A hearing with judges and plans seems to be about the rebuilding, but I am not sure.
tra_loi.Q6: A large white cathedral with a big dome (St Paul's, 1708–1711) rises above the red-roofed houses. The caption says 'The dome rules the skyline', and a '365 ft' label appears. A tall column or monument also appears in the pictures, but I am not sure which frame shows it clearly.
tra_loi.Q7: On 29 Dec 1940 aircraft or airships fly over and the city burns again at night (a 'second great fire'). Firefighters work on the riverbank and on rooftops. A 'killed' counter (160) appears, and a large area is shown burned, with the 1941 map marking the damaged zone. The dome of St Paul's survives, shown with a ring around it in 1938 and in the snowy 1942 photo. The streets are rebuilt again on the same layout (1946, 'Second rebuilding, same streets').
tra_loi.Q8: Today (2026) it is a dense modern city of grey and brick office and apartment blocks and glass skyscrapers beside the river, with bridges. The dome of St Paul's can still be seen among the towers. The old street layout is still there, and the film ends by cutting back to the 1666 fire and to text about how it was made.

tra_loi.Q1: A great fire. Dated 2 Sept 1666 and titled "1666 — The Great Fire", it burns timber-built houses along the river and spreads for several days.
tra_loi.Q2: It begins in one small place. The baker's oven and fire in a bakery (Thomas Farriner, baker to the King) is followed by flames in a narrow street of timber houses, then the blaze grows block by block. A map later shows the burned area, with Pudding Lane and the Royal Exchange marked.
tra_loi.Q3: They flee on foot and by cart with bundles of belongings, and escape by boat on the river. Men pull down houses with hooks to make firebreaks. Some bury valuables in a garden pit. Survivors then camp in open fields with tents and carts.
tra_loi.Q4: The old church on the hill (Old St Paul's) catches fire on 4 Sept. Its windows burn and molten lead runs down the walls and across the street, and the roof burns away. The church is left as a ruin, with a toppled statue among the rubble.
tra_loi.Q5: Rebuilding is in red brick, with scaffolding, carts and bricklayers, and later row after row of red-roofed brick houses. The layout is the old medieval street pattern ("Rebuilding on the old streets"), not the new grand plan shown on the map. Court scenes appear as well.
tra_loi.Q6: A large white domed cathedral (St Paul's, with its dome finished in 1711, shown as a tall "365 ft" structure) rises above the red roofs. A tall column also appears, but I can't tell for sure which one it is from the pictures. It may be the thin column seen in the 1670s–80s aerial views, and I'm not certain.
tra_loi.Q7: On 29 Dec 1940 bombers and airships come over, and the city burns at night. Firefighters with hoses fight the fires, and the Gothic church burns. A damaged-area map is shown, with a "160 killed" count. St Paul's with its dome survives and stands out through the smoke and in the photo dated 1942.
tra_loi.Q8: A modern 2026 city of grey and glass blocks and skyscrapers, with bridges over the river. Among the towers, St Paul's dome is still visible. The film ends with a night view of lit buildings and then "how this film was made" text.
